subject: Montague AI sustained queue jams — Private VPC (urgent executive brief)
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@montague.ai>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-07T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Montague private VPC - sustained latency and queue growth

Hi Laura / Marissa,

We're seeing a sudden and sustained increase in tail latency for our Private VPC deployment (cluster: montague-vpc-prod, region: us-west-2) beginning ~2027-09-07 04:00 UTC. Quick summary: p95 rose from ~220ms to ~1.3s, p99 spikes to ~3.2s, and 5xx error rate has climbed to ~0.8%. Throughput requests/sec is roughly steady, but the request queue length on the load balancer has been growing and consumer batch windows are widening.

We sampled 30 minutes of traces and attached the tail trace and a small CSV of KV miss samples. Early look shows a sharp rise in KV cache miss rate (from ~3% baseline to ~37% during spikes). We also observed short disk stalls on the local NVMe (~50-200ms micro-pauses) coincident with decode stalls.

This is impacting our critical inference endpoints (real-time chat & webhook scoring). Customer ops are seeing user complaints and are asking for a remediation plan and ETA. We're attaching the logs: montague_tailtrace_0907.log and kv_miss_sampling_0907.csv.

Request: please triage and tell us whether this is a Redwood runtime regression, model layer fallback (quant->fp32), or an infra-level GC/IO issue.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Platform, Montague AI

Attachments: montague_tailtrace_0907.log (text), kv_miss_sampling_0907.csv (csv)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Elena Rossi <elena@montague.ai>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-09-07T08:38:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Montague private VPC - sustained latency and queue growth

Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We see the same correlations in our telemetry. Looping in Jonas (serving runtime) and Karthik (customer success / account) to triage immediately.

Immediate asks:
- Jonas: can you confirm whether the increased KV miss rate is coming from prefix eviction or a cache key namespace change after the last rollout?
- Can we get a small sample of process-level NVMe latencies from the nodes (iostat/blkstat) and the worker logs for the period 03:45-04:30 UTC?
- Marissa: please keep Montague ops in the loop with a high-level timeline; do not commit to any SLA credits yet.

If this looks like an infra-level stall (NVMe GC or kernel-level pause), we may need an emergency rolling restart of the worker pool. If it's a runtime regression, we will prepare a hotfix.

I'll coordinate an internal bridge and update you within 60 minutes.

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Montague private VPC - sustained latency and queue growth

On Tue, Sep 7, 2027 at 08:38 AM laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We see the same correlations in our telemetry. Looping in Jonas (serving runtime) and Karthik (customer success / account) to triage immediately.

Initial technical notes after a 30-minute triage:
- KV cache miss storm: there are many cold-key fetches for long-tail prompts; miss ratio matches the CSV Elena attached. This amplifies backend decoding work per request.
- Local NVMe micro-pauses: observed short (~50-250ms) stalls on 4 nodes (blk-iostat). Stalls align with p99 windows and with internal checkpoint flushes on one node.
- Model fallback: no evidence of a quant->fp32 fallback in the model logs; decoding time increase is consistent with more tokens being re-decoded due to cache misses and longer batching windows.

Immediate mitigations I propose (low-risk, can be applied without code deploy):
1) Temporarily reduce the batch window from 80ms -> 20ms for the affected route to prevent window amplification.
2) Enable aggressive KV prefetching for hot key prefixes (heuristic-based) — config change only.
3) Offload non-critical routes to a lower priority pool / suggest temporary fallback to Redwood-hosted endpoints for critical customers if they opt-in.
4) Plan a rolling restart of the 4 implicated nodes to clear the NVMe stall state (requires customer approval for maintenance window).

I will stage the config changes right away and monitor for improvement. If there's no material improvement within 2 hours, we should schedule the rolling restart during a coordinated maintenance window.

—Jonas
Sr Staff, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

- Short-term mitigations (in flight): Jonas will apply batch-window reduction and KV prefetching now.
- Outstanding decision: Montague requests permission for an emergency rolling restart of 4 nodes (expected ~15-20m per node drain, potential transient request retries). Procurement has flagged the need for written approval if we call this "maintenance."
- Business risk: Marissa, please estimate commercial exposure. Early ballpark: up to ~$45k/day in credits (TBD). We need a one-pager for execs with the remediation timeline and decision points.

Action items:
- Jonas: short exec-friendly remediation summary (1 page) + rollback plan. Due: 90 minutes.
- Marissa: customer-facing timeline & commercial exposure estimate. Due: 90 minutes.
- Karthik: sign-off path for authorizing emergency maintenance and any contract deviation.

If we do not see a >40% reduction in p99 within 2 hours after config changes, I want permission to notify our CEO and schedule a CEO-to-CEO call with Montague to acknowledge the issue and proposed remediation.

—Laura Bennett
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
